name: M&T Bank Corp.
reason: Conservative long-record underwriter with a low-cost deposit franchise; EPS 10y CAGR 9.0% with only a -27.7% worst year (2020) and consensus FY2-3 ~8%, though EPS sits at its 10y peak and CRE exposure needs checking in deep dive.

name: VF Corp.
reason: Brand turnaround with EPS down 11.7%/yr over 10y (0.24x 10y peak), margin 7.0% vs 18.0% peak and net debt/EBITDA 3.2x; not forecastable and not special.

name: BOK Financial Corp.
reason: Decent bank (EPS CAGR 8.1%) but earnings lean on energy lending, mortgage and trading/fixed-income fee lines tied to rate and commodity cycles; EPS at 10y high and FY2 consensus growth only 1.1%.

name: Valero Energy Corp.
reason: Refiner whose earnings are set by crack spreads (EPS swung from -3.12 to 29.16 in two years); commodity-driven and unforecastable.

name: Capital Southwest Corp
reason: Internally managed BDC whose income is set by middle-market credit and base rates; share count compounding 15.4%/yr and consensus EPS flat to down.

name: Newell Brands, Inc.
reason: Acquisition-built consumer goods roll-up with EPS down 12.6%/yr, net debt/EBITDA 6.1x and acq/FCF 1.83x; fails balance-sheet and growth tests.

name: G-III Apparel Group Ltd.
reason: Licensed-apparel wholesaler facing loss of PVH (Calvin Klein/Tommy) licences; EPS 10y CAGR 0.7% and consensus FY1 -13.8%, a single-licensor threat.

name: The PNC Financial Services Group, Inc.
reason: Large ordinary super-regional whose growth has come via acquisitions (BBVA USA, FirstBank); 5y EPS CAGR -0.4% and EPS at 0.98x 10y peak; cheap but not special.

name: T. Rowe Price Group, Inc.
reason: Active asset manager in secular outflow to passive with margin down from 49.9% to 35.4% and consensus EPS growth ~0% FY2-3; earnings set by market levels.

name: UMB Financial Corp.
reason: Best-in-batch organic record (EPS 10y CAGR 15.9%, 9/10 years >=7%, worst year -8.3%) with differentiated fee franchises (fund services, HSA); 2025 Heartland deal lifted shares (+4.5%/yr) so integration must be checked.

name: Republic Bancorp, Inc. (Kentucky)
reason: Solid EPS record (10y CAGR 14.7%) but a material share of profits comes from tax refund solutions, prepaid and warehouse mortgage lending that hinge on regulation and partner relationships.

name: Occidental Petroleum Corp.
reason: Oil & gas E&P plus commodity chemicals; EPS set by oil prices (0.24x 10y peak, 2/9 years of >=7% growth) and Anadarko deal drove acq/FCF 1.05x.

name: CNA Financial Corp.
reason: Average commercial P&C underwriter controlled by Loews with legacy long-tail reserves; EPS at 10y peak and long-term growth consensus only 2.1%.

name: United Community Banks, Inc.
reason: Southeast bank grown by serial acquisitions (shares +6.4%/yr vs EPS +7.9%/yr), with 2023 EPS -20.7%; ordinary franchise without specialness.

name: Micron Technology, Inc.
reason: Commodity memory maker at an extreme cyclical peak: EPS 75.52 at 1.0x 10y max with EBIT margin 75% (100th pctile) after -33% margin in 2023.

name: Flex Ltd.
reason: Contract manufacturer with thin 5.4% EBIT margin at a 10y high (100th pctile) on an AI/data-centre power upcycle and negative 10y FCF conversion (-0.23); customer-concentrated and hard to forecast.

name: Central Garden & Pet Co.
reason: Pet/garden consumables with steady EPS growth (10y CAGR 16.8%) but margin at 10y high (8.5%), weather-driven garden segment and acquisition-fed growth (acq/FCF 0.72x).

name: LiveRamp Holdings, Inc.
reason: Identity/data-collaboration software exposed to privacy regulation and cookie/ID deprecation; adjusted EPS far above GAAP (gap 365%) and revenue CAGR -0.4% since Acxiom split.

name: Asbury Automotive Group, Inc.
reason: Auto dealer whose growth came from acquisitions (acq/FCF 2.45x) and leverage (net debt/EBITDA 5.5x) with EPS 0.75x the 2022 peak as used/new GPUs normalise.

name: Commerce Bancshares, Inc. (Missouri)
reason: Family-led, conservatively underwritten bank with low-cost deposits, strong fee businesses (cards, trust), zero acquisition spend and ROE 14.5%; EPS 10y CAGR 9.9% with consensus ~9% FY2-3.
